source.text: וּמַֽלְכַּת־שְׁבָ֗א שֹׁמַ֛עַת אֶת־שֵׁ֥מַע שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה לְשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֑ה וַתָּבֹ֥א לְנַסֹּת֖וֹ בְּחִידֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] queen of Sheba [was] hearing [the] report of Solomon concerning [the] name of Yahweh, and she came to test him with riddles.

en.L: And the queen of Sheba heard the report of Solomon concerning the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and she came to test him with riddles.
en.B: The queen of Sheba heard of Solomon's fame, a fame bound up with the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and she came to test him with difficult questions.
en.R: The queen of Sheba heard how famous Solomon was, and that his fame had to do with the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. So she came to test him with hard questions.

decisions.choice: Sheba: a trading kingdom in the south of Arabia
decisions.reason: Sheba lay in the south-west of the Arabian peninsula. It grew rich on the caravan trade in incense, spices, gold and precious stones, the very goods the queen brings in verse 2 (Genesis 10:7, 28; Psalm 72:10, 15; Isaiah 60:6; Jeremiah 6:20).

decisions.choice: the report of Solomon concerning the name of Yahweh: Solomon's fame, which was tied to the name of Yahweh
alternatives: the report of Solomon, and of the name of Yahweh
the fame Solomon had won for the name of Yahweh
decisions.reason: The phrase is short and unusual. It most likely means that what the queen heard about Solomon was bound up with Yahweh: he had built the house for Yahweh's name (8:17-20), and Solomon had prayed that foreigners would come because they heard of that name (8:41-43). The parallel account in 2 Chronicles 9:1 does not have the words about the name.

decisions.choice: riddles: hard, puzzling questions
decisions.reason: The word names a riddle or an enigma that has to be worked out (Judges 14:12-19; Proverbs 1:6; Psalm 49:5). Testing a ruler with such questions was a way to probe his wisdom, the gift Yahweh gave Solomon (3:12; 5:9-14).

decisions.choice: riddles (Literal); difficult questions (Balanced); hard questions (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the narrow sense of the word. "Riddles" can sound like children's games, so Balanced and Readable say "questions", the way the queen uses them: to test what Solomon knows.

source.text: וַתָּבֹ֣א יְרוּשָׁלְַ֗מָה בְּחַיִל֮ כָּבֵ֣ד מְאֹד֒ גְּ֠מַלִּים נֹשְׂאִ֨ים בְּשָׂמִ֧ים וְזָהָ֛ב רַב־מְאֹ֖ד וְאֶ֣בֶן יְקָרָ֑ה וַתָּבֹא֙ אֶל־שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה וַתְּדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלָ֔יו אֵ֛ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיָ֖ה עִם־לְבָבָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And she came to Jerusalem with [a] retinue heavy very, camels carrying spices and gold much very and stone precious; and she came to Solomon and she spoke to him all that was with her heart.

en.L: And she came to Jerusalem with a very heavy retinue, camels carrying spices and very much gold and precious stones; and she came to Solomon and spoke to him all that was with her heart.
en.B: She arrived in Jerusalem with a very large company, with camels carrying spices, a great quantity of gold, and precious stones. When she came to Solomon, she talked with him about everything she had on her mind.
en.R: She arrived in Jerusalem with a huge group of attendants. Her camels were loaded with spices, large amounts of gold, and valuable jewels. She came to Solomon and asked him about everything she had been thinking about.

decisions.choice: a very heavy retinue: a large and impressive company of attendants
decisions.reason: The word can mean strength, wealth, or an army. Here it names the people, animals and goods that travel with the queen, a show of her rank and wealth; "heavy" means great in number.

decisions.choice: all that was with her heart: everything she had in mind to ask
decisions.reason: The heart is the seat of thought in Hebrew. She lays before Solomon all the questions she had prepared (verse 1).

decisions.choice: camels carrying spices: the caravan trade of Arabia
decisions.reason: Camel caravans carried incense and spices north from southern Arabia along the desert routes. The queen arrives with the goods her land was known for.

decisions.choice: a huge group of attendants; valuable jewels
decisions.reason: Readable names who made up the company and says "jewels" for "precious stones", the plainer word for gems.

source.text: וַיַּגֶּד־לָ֥הּ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה אֶת־כָּל־דְּבָרֶ֑יהָ לֹֽא־הָיָ֤ה דָּבָר֙ נֶעְלָ֣ם מִן־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֧ר לֹ֦א הִגִּ֖יד לָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And told her Solomon all her words; not was [a] word hidden from the king which not he told her.

en.L: And Solomon told her all her words; there was not a thing hidden from the king that he did not tell her.
en.B: Solomon answered all her questions; nothing was too hidden for the king to explain to her.
en.R: Solomon answered every one of her questions. None of them was too hard for the king to explain.

decisions.choice: told her all her words: answered every question she put to him
decisions.reason: The verb means to tell or make known. With "her words", the questions she raised, it means that Solomon gave her the answer to each one.

decisions.choice: hidden from the king: beyond his understanding
decisions.reason: A matter "hidden" from someone is one he cannot see into. None of her riddles was beyond Solomon's grasp.

decisions.choice: answered; explain
decisions.reason: The same verb appears twice. Balanced and Readable say "answered" for the first, since she had asked questions, and "explain" for the second, which is what telling the answer to a riddle means.

source.text: וַתֵּ֨רֶא֙ מַֽלְכַּת־שְׁבָ֔א אֵ֖ת כָּל־חָכְמַ֣ת שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה וְהַבַּ֖יִת אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw [the] queen of Sheba all [the] wisdom of Solomon and the house which he built,

en.L: And the queen of Sheba saw all the wisdom of Solomon, and the house that he had built,
en.B: When the queen of Sheba saw the full extent of Solomon's wisdom, and the palace he had built,
en.R: The queen of Sheba saw for herself how wise Solomon was. She saw the palace he had built.

decisions.choice: saw: the sentence runs on to the end of verse 5
decisions.reason: Verses 4 and 5 are one sentence: a long list of what the queen saw, ending with how it affected her ("there was no more spirit in her").

decisions.choice: the house that he had built: Solomon's palace
decisions.reason: "House" can mean a palace or a temple. Since the house of Yahweh is named at the end of verse 5, this house is most likely the royal palace, which took Solomon thirteen years to build (7:1-12).

decisions.choice: the wisdom of Solomon: the wisdom Yahweh gave him
decisions.reason: The queen sees with her own eyes what Yahweh promised at Gibeon (3:12): a wise and understanding heart greater than any before or after.

decisions.choice: palace
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "palace" for "house", so that readers do not take it for the house of the LORD.

source.text: וּמַאֲכַ֣ל שֻׁלְחָנ֡וֹ וּמוֹשַׁ֣ב עֲבָדָיו֩ וּמַעֲמַ֨ד מְשָׁרְתָ֜יו וּמַלְבֻּֽשֵׁיהֶם֙ וּמַשְׁקָ֔יו וְעֹ֣לָת֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַעֲלֶ֖ה בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה וְלֹא־הָ֥יָה בָ֛הּ ע֖וֹד רֽוּחַ׃

records.literal_gloss: and [the] food of his table, and [the] seating of his servants, and [the] standing of his attendants and their clothing, and his cupbearers, and his burnt offering which he offered up [at the] house of Yahweh, and not was in her still spirit.

en.L: and the food of his table, and the seating of his servants, and the standing of his attendants and their clothing, and his cupbearers, and his burnt offerings that he offered up [at the] house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, then there was no more spirit in her.
en.B: the food on his table, the seating of his officials, the service of his attendants and their robes, his cupbearers, and the burnt offerings he offered at the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, she was left breathless.
en.R: She saw the food on his table, the way his officials were seated, how his servants waited on him, and the fine clothes they wore. She saw his cupbearers, and the burnt offerings he sacrificed at the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. It all took her breath away.

decisions.choice: there was no more spirit in her: she was overwhelmed
decisions.reason: "Spirit" here is breath and strength. To have no spirit left is to be stunned or overcome, as the kings of Canaan were when they heard what Yahweh had done (Joshua 2:11; 5:1). Here it is amazement, not fear.

decisions.choice: his burnt offerings that he offered up at the house of Yahweh
alternatives: the stairway by which he went up to the house of Yahweh
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word can be read as "his burnt offering" or, with different vowels, as "his ascent". The parallel in 2 Chronicles 9:4 has a related word meaning "his going up", and some ancient translations read "the stairway by which he went up to the house of Yahweh". The Hebrew text of Kings as it stands reads "burnt offering", and the verb "offered up" is the one used for sacrifices.

decisions.choice: his servants, his attendants, his cupbearers: the members of Solomon's court
decisions.reason: "Servants" here are the king's officials, seated in order at his table. The attendants stood ready to serve, and the cupbearers served the king's wine, a post of trust at a royal court (Genesis 40:1-2; Nehemiah 1:11).

decisions.choice: officials
decisions.reason: As with the king's servants elsewhere in Samuel and Kings, Balanced and Readable say "officials" for men who held posts at court.

decisions.choice: she was left breathless (Balanced); It all took her breath away (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew picture. Balanced and Readable use the English idiom of breath, which keeps both the picture and the sense of being overwhelmed.

source.text: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֱמֶת֙ הָיָ֣ה הַדָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁמַ֖עְתִּי בְּאַרְצִ֑י עַל־דְּבָרֶ֖יךָ וְעַל־חָכְמָתֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And she said to the king, Truth was the word which I heard in my land about your words and about your wisdom.

en.L: And she said to the king, "True was the word that I heard in my land about your words and about your wisdom.
en.B: She said to the king, "It was true, the report that reached me in my own country about your words and your wisdom.
en.R: She said to the king, "Everything I heard in my own country about what you have said and how wise you are is true.

decisions.choice: true was the report: the word "truth" comes first for emphasis
decisions.reason: The queen begins with the word "truth". What she had heard and half doubted (verse 7) has proved true.

decisions.choice: your words: what Solomon said
decisions.reason: The word can mean words or matters. Paired with "your wisdom" and following her questions (verse 3), it most likely means his sayings and answers, though it could also take in his affairs and achievements.

decisions.choice: word (Literal); report (Balanced); Everything I heard (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word for "word" here means a report, as the same verb "heard" shows. Balanced says "report" and Readable puts it as what she heard.

source.text: וְלֹֽא־הֶאֱמַ֣נְתִּי לַדְּבָרִ֗ים עַ֤ד אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֨אתִי֙ וַתִּרְאֶ֣ינָה עֵינַ֔י וְהִנֵּ֥ה לֹֽא־הֻגַּד־לִ֖י הַחֵ֑צִי הוֹסַ֤פְתָּ חָכְמָה֙ וָט֔וֹב אֶל־הַשְּׁמוּעָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁמָֽעְתִּי׃

records.literal_gloss: And not I believed the words until that I came and saw my eyes, and look, not was told to me the half; you have added wisdom and good to the report which I heard.

en.L: And I did not believe the words until I came and my eyes saw; and look, the half was not told to me. You have added wisdom and good beyond the report that I heard.
en.B: But I did not believe what was said until I came and saw it with my own eyes. And indeed, I was not told even half. Your wisdom and prosperity go far beyond the report I heard.
en.R: But I did not believe it until I came and saw it for myself. Now I see that they did not tell me even half of it! You are far wiser and richer than the reports I heard.

decisions.choice: look: she points to what she now sees
decisions.reason: The small word draws attention to something seen or realized. The queen turns from what she heard to what is before her eyes.

decisions.choice: good: prosperity, wealth
decisions.reason: "Good" here is set beside "wisdom" and refers to all the good things she has seen in verses 4-5: the wealth and splendor of Solomon's court.

decisions.choice: you have added beyond the report: you surpass what was said of you
decisions.reason: To "add to" a report is to go beyond it. The reality is more than the rumor.

decisions.choice: indeed (Balanced); Now I see (Readable)
decisions.reason: Neither level uses the old word "behold". Balanced says "indeed" and Readable puts her surprise in her own words.

source.text: אַשְׁרֵ֣י אֲנָשֶׁ֔יךָ אַשְׁרֵ֖י עֲבָדֶ֣יךָ אֵ֑לֶּה הָֽעֹמְדִ֤ים לְפָנֶ֨יךָ֙ תָּמִ֔יד הַשֹּׁמְעִ֖ים אֶת־חָכְמָתֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Happy your men, happy your servants these, the standing before you continually, the hearing your wisdom.

en.L: Happy [are] your men, happy [are] these your servants who stand before you continually, who hear your wisdom.
en.B: How happy your men must be! How happy are these officials of yours, who stand before you all the time and hear your wisdom!
en.R: How fortunate your men are! How fortunate these officials are, who are always with you and get to hear your wisdom!

decisions.choice: happy: fortunate, well off
decisions.reason: The word describes a person whose lot is good (Psalm 1:1). It is not the word for being blessed by God that the queen uses in verse 9.

decisions.choice: your men
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text has "your men", as does the parallel in 2 Chronicles 9:7. The ancient Greek translation has "your wives", which differs by one letter in Hebrew. The Hebrew reading fits the next line, about the officials who serve the king.

decisions.choice: who stand before you: who serve you
decisions.reason: To stand before a king is to be in his service, waiting on his word (1:2; 12:8).

decisions.choice: officials
decisions.reason: As in verse 5, Balanced and Readable say "officials" for the king's servants at court.

source.text: יְהִ֨י יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ בָּר֔וּךְ אֲשֶׁר֙ חָפֵ֣ץ בְּךָ֔ לְתִתְּךָ֖ עַל־כִּסֵּ֣א יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל בְּאַהֲבַ֨ת יְהוָ֤ה אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לְעֹלָ֔ם וַיְשִֽׂימְךָ֣ לְמֶ֔לֶךְ לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת מִשְׁפָּ֖ט וּצְדָקָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: May be Yahweh your God blessed, who delighted in you to set you on [the] throne of Israel; in [the] loving of Yahweh Israel forever, and he set you as king to do justice and righteousness.

en.L: May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God be blessed, who delighted in you to set you on the throne of Israel! Because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} loved Israel forever, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made you king to do justice and righteousness."
en.B: Blessed be {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, who has delighted in you and set you on the throne of Israel! Because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} loves Israel forever, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made you king, to do justice and righteousness."
en.R: Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God! He was pleased with you and put you on the throne of Israel. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} loves Israel forever, so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made you king to rule with justice and righteousness."

decisions.choice: may Yahweh your God be blessed: a foreign queen praises Israel's God
decisions.reason: The queen speaks of Yahweh as Solomon's God, not hers, but she blesses him and credits him with Solomon's rule, as Hiram of Tyre did (5:21). It answers Solomon's prayer that foreigners would come because of Yahweh's name (8:41-43).

decisions.choice: because Yahweh loves Israel forever: the king is a gift to the people
decisions.reason: She sees Solomon's throne as a sign of Yahweh's lasting love, not for Solomon alone but for Israel. The king exists for the people's good.

decisions.choice: to do justice and righteousness: to rule fairly and rightly
decisions.reason: The pair describes what a king is for: fair judgment and right dealing for all, especially the weak (2 Samuel 8:15; Psalm 72:1-4). Solomon had asked for this ability at Gibeon (3:9).

decisions.choice: Praise
decisions.reason: Readable says "Praise" for "blessed" here, since in English a person can praise God but "bless" him sounds like giving him something. It keeps the same act of thanks and honor.

decisions.choice: he made you king
decisions.reason: The Hebrew joins the clause with "and" after the reason ("because Yahweh loves Israel ... and he set you"). English drops the "and", which would break the sentence, and the queen's speech that began in verse 6 closes here.

source.text: וַתִּתֵּ֨ן לַמֶּ֜לֶךְ מֵאָ֥ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֣ים׀כִּכַּ֣ר זָהָ֗ב וּבְשָׂמִ֛ים הַרְבֵּ֥ה מְאֹ֖ד וְאֶ֣בֶן יְקָרָ֑ה לֹא־בָא֩ כַבֹּ֨שֶׂם הַה֥וּא עוֹד֙ לָרֹ֔ב אֲשֶׁר־נָתְנָ֥ה מַֽלְכַּת־שְׁבָ֖א לַמֶּ֥לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And she gave to the king hundred and twenty talent[s] of gold, and spices much very, and stone precious; not came like the spice that again in abundance which gave [the] queen of Sheba to the king Solomon.

en.L: And she gave to the king 120 talents of gold, and very many spices, and precious stones. There never again came spice like that in abundance, which the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.
en.B: Then she gave the king {{units:about 9,000 pounds|120 talents}} of gold, a very great quantity of spices, and precious stones. Never again did such an abundance of spices come in as the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.
en.R: She gave the king {{units:about 9,000 pounds|120 talents}} of gold, huge amounts of spices, and valuable jewels. No one ever again brought in as many spices as the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.

decisions.choice: 120 talents of gold: a royal gift of great size
decisions.reason: A talent was the largest unit of weight, about 75 pounds, so the gold weighed about 9,000 pounds. Gifts between rulers showed honor and wealth on both sides; Hiram gave Solomon the same amount (9:14).

decisions.choice: never again came spice like that in abundance: the amount of her gift was never matched
decisions.reason: The comparison is about quantity: no later shipment of spices to Israel equaled hers.

decisions.choice: about 9,000 pounds (talents as the alternative)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the weight in modern measure, with the Hebrew unit as the alternative; Literal keeps "talents".

decisions.choice: No one ever again brought in
decisions.reason: Readable turns "there never came" into a sentence with a subject, which is easier to follow.

source.text: וְגַם֙ אֳנִ֣י חִירָ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־נָשָׂ֥א זָהָ֖ב מֵאוֹפִ֑יר הֵבִ֨יא מֵאֹפִ֜יר עֲצֵ֧י אַלְמֻגִּ֛ים הַרְבֵּ֥ה מְאֹ֖ד וְאֶ֥בֶן יְקָרָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And also [the] ships of Hiram which carried gold from Ophir brought from Ophir wood of almug much very and stone precious.

en.L: And also the ships of Hiram, which carried gold from Ophir, brought from Ophir very much almug wood and precious stones.
en.B: Hiram's fleet, which carried gold from Ophir, also brought from Ophir a great quantity of almug wood and precious stones.
en.R: Hiram's ships, which brought gold from Ophir, also brought back large amounts of almug wood and valuable jewels.

decisions.choice: the ships of Hiram: the fleet that sailed for Solomon from the Red Sea
decisions.reason: Solomon built ships at Ezion-geber on the Red Sea, and Hiram king of Tyre sent experienced sailors to crew them with Solomon's men (9:26-28). The fleet is called Hiram's because his men sailed it.

decisions.choice: Ophir: a distant land famous for gold
decisions.reason: Where Ophir lay is not known. Places in southern Arabia, east Africa and India have all been suggested. Its gold was a byword for the finest (Job 28:16; Psalm 45:10).

decisions.choice: almug wood: a costly wood that cannot be identified with certainty
decisions.reason: The word appears only here and in verse 12. The parallel in 2 Chronicles 9:10-11 spells it "algum". It was a fine wood fit for temple work and musical instruments; red sandalwood is one suggestion, but no identification is sure.

decisions.choice: brought back
decisions.reason: Readable says "brought back" and drops the repeated "from Ophir", since the ships are already said to sail from there.

source.text: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ הַ֠מֶּלֶךְ אֶת־עֲצֵ֨י הָאַלְמֻגִּ֜ים מִסְעָ֤ד לְבֵית־יְהוָה֙ וּלְבֵ֣ית הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְכִנֹּר֥וֹת וּנְבָלִ֖ים לַשָּׁרִ֑ים לֹ֣א בָֽא־כֵ֞ן עֲצֵ֤י אַלְמֻגִּים֙ וְלֹ֣א נִרְאָ֔ה עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And made the king the wood of the almug supports for [the] house of Yahweh and for [the] house of the king, and lyres and harps for the singers; not came thus wood of almug and not was seen until the day the this.

en.L: And the king made the almug wood [into] supports for the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and for the house of the king, and lyres and harps for the singers. Such almug wood has not come, and has not been seen, to this day.
en.B: The king used the almug wood to make supports for the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the royal palace, as well as lyres and harps for the singers. No such almug wood has come in again or been seen to this day.
en.R: The king used the almug wood to make supports for the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and for the royal palace. He also made lyres and harps for the musicians. No almug wood like it has ever come in again, and none has been seen to this day.

decisions.choice: supports: some part of the buildings made of the wood, perhaps railings or steps
decisions.reason: The word appears only here, and its exact sense is unknown. It comes from a verb meaning to support or hold up, so it may mean supports, railings or a stair. The parallel in 2 Chronicles 9:11 has a different word that may mean steps or terraces.

decisions.choice: lyres and harps: the stringed instruments of temple and court music
decisions.reason: Both are stringed instruments played by hand; the second was probably larger. David had appointed singers with such instruments for worship (1 Chronicles 15:16).

decisions.choice: to this day: the writer's own day
decisions.reason: As at 8:8, the writer speaks from his own time, long after Solomon: no such wood had come in since.

decisions.choice: the temple of the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable says "temple" for the house of the LORD, as it does elsewhere in 1 Kings, and "musicians" for the singers who played these instruments.

source.text: וְהַמֶּ֨לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה נָתַ֣ן לְמַֽלְכַּת־שְׁבָ֗א אֶת־כָּל־חֶפְצָהּ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁאָ֔לָה מִלְּבַד֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָֽתַן־לָ֔הּ כְּיַ֖ד הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה וַתֵּ֛פֶן וַתֵּ֥לֶךְ לְאַרְצָ֖הּ הִ֥יא וַעֲבָדֶֽיהָ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And the king Solomon gave to [the] queen of Sheba all her desire which she asked, besides what he gave to her according to [the] hand of the king Solomon; and she turned and went to her land, she and her servants.

en.L: And King Solomon gave to the queen of Sheba all her desire that she asked, besides what he gave her according to the hand of King Solomon. And she turned and went to her land, she and her servants.
en.B: King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba everything she desired and asked for, on top of the gifts he had given her out of his royal bounty. Then she turned and went back to her own country, she and her servants.
en.R: King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba everything she wanted and asked for. This was in addition to all the gifts he had already given her from his royal wealth. Then she and her servants went back home to her own country.

decisions.choice: according to the hand of King Solomon: as befitted a king of his wealth
decisions.reason: "Hand" here stands for a person's means and generosity. Solomon gave her gifts in keeping with his royal wealth, on top of what she asked for.

decisions.choice: all her desire that she asked: gifts in return for gifts
decisions.reason: Rulers exchanged gifts as a sign of honor and friendship. The queen had given lavishly (verse 10), and Solomon gave her whatever she asked and more.

decisions.choice: out of his royal bounty (Balanced); from his royal wealth (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable explain the idiom of the hand rather than reproduce it.

source.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ מִשְׁקַ֣ל הַזָּהָ֔ב אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֥א לִשְׁלֹמֹ֖ה בְּשָׁנָ֣ה אֶחָ֑ת שֵׁ֥שׁ מֵא֛וֹת שִׁשִּׁ֥ים וָשֵׁ֖שׁ כִּכַּ֥ר זָהָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And was [the] weight of the gold which came to Solomon in year one six hundred sixty and six talent[s] of gold,

en.L: And the weight of the gold that came to Solomon in one year was 666 talents of gold,
en.B: The weight of the gold that came to Solomon in one year was {{units:about 50,000 pounds|666 talents}} of gold,
en.R: In one year the gold that came to Solomon weighed {{units:about 25 tons|666 talents}}.

decisions.choice: in one year: Solomon's yearly income in gold
decisions.reason: The phrase most likely gives what came in during a single year as a regular amount, though it could describe one particular year. The sentence continues into verse 15, which adds income not counted in this figure.

decisions.choice: 666 talents: a vast weight of gold
decisions.reason: At about 75 pounds to the talent, this is about 50,000 pounds, about 25 tons. The figure is given as a weight of gold, part of the picture of Solomon's wealth in verses 14-29.

decisions.choice: about 50,000 pounds (Balanced); about 25 tons (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the weight in modern measure, with the Hebrew unit as the alternative; Readable rounds it to tons, an easier figure to picture. Readable ends the sentence here and starts verse 15 with its own.

source.text: לְבַד֙ מֵאַנְשֵׁ֣י הַתָּרִ֔ים וּמִסְחַ֖ר הָרֹכְלִ֑ים וְכָל־מַלְכֵ֥י הָעֶ֖רֶב וּפַח֥וֹת הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: apart from [the] men of the traders and [the] trade of the merchants, and all [the] kings of the Arabs and [the] governors of the land.

en.L: apart from [what came] from the men of the traders and the trade of the merchants, and [from] all the kings of the Arabs and the governors of the land.
en.B: not counting what came from the traveling traders and the business of the merchants, and from all the kings of Arabia and the governors of the land.
en.R: That did not include what he received from traders and merchants, from all the kings of Arabia, and from the governors of the land.

decisions.choice: the traders and the merchants: the trade that passed through Solomon's land
decisions.reason: The first word means men who travel about, here traveling traders; the second names dealers in goods. Solomon took income from the trade routes that ran through his kingdom.

decisions.choice: the Arabs: the kings of the Arabian peoples
decisions.reason: The parallel in 2 Chronicles 9:14 reads "Arabia". The same Hebrew letters can be read as "the mixed peoples", as in Jeremiah 25:20, 24, and some ancient translations read "across the river". The kings of Arabia fit the trade of this chapter.

decisions.choice: the governors of the land: officials over districts or provinces
decisions.reason: The word names a governor of a region. These may be Solomon's own district officers (4:7-19) or rulers of lands under his control.

decisions.choice: what came from
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "apart from the men of the traders"; English needs words saying that it was their payments that were not counted. Literal puts them in brackets.

source.text: וַיַּ֨עַשׂ הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֛ה מָאתַ֥יִם צִנָּ֖ה זָהָ֣ב שָׁח֑וּט שֵׁשׁ־מֵא֣וֹת זָהָ֔ב יַעֲלֶ֖ה עַל־הַצִּנָּ֥ה הָאֶחָֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And made the king Solomon two hundred large-shield[s] gold beaten; six hundred gold he put up on the large-shield the one.

en.L: And King Solomon made 200 large shields of beaten gold; 600 [shekels of] gold he put on each large shield.
en.B: King Solomon made 200 large shields of beaten gold, with {{units:about 15 pounds|600 shekels}} of gold going into each shield.
en.R: King Solomon made 200 large shields of hammered gold. Each one used {{units:about 15 pounds|600 shekels}} of gold.

decisions.choice: large shields: tall shields that covered the whole body
decisions.reason: This word names the large shield that protected a soldier from head to foot, unlike the smaller round shield of verse 17.

decisions.choice: of beaten gold: gold hammered into sheets, likely over a frame
decisions.reason: The gold was beaten thin and laid on the shield, probably over wood or leather. These were ceremonial shields carried by the royal guard (14:26-28), a display of wealth rather than equipment for battle.

decisions.choice: six hundred of gold: 600 shekels
decisions.reason: The Hebrew gives only the number. The unit understood is the shekel, the common weight for such amounts.

decisions.choice: shekels
decisions.reason: Literal supplies "shekels" in brackets; Balanced and Readable give the weight, about 15 pounds, with "600 shekels" as the alternative.

source.text: וּשְׁלֹשׁ־מֵא֤וֹת מָֽגִנִּים֙ זָהָ֣ב שָׁח֔וּט שְׁלֹ֤שֶׁת מָנִים֙ זָהָ֔ב יַעֲלֶ֖ה עַל־הַמָּגֵ֣ן הָאֶחָ֑ת וַיִּתְּנֵ֣ם הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ בֵּ֖ית יַ֥עַר הַלְּבָנֽוֹן׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And three hundred shields gold beaten; three minas gold he put up on the shield the one; and put them the king [in the] house of [the] forest of the Lebanon.

en.L: And 300 shields of beaten gold; three minas of gold he put on each shield. And the king put them [in the] house of the forest of Lebanon.
en.B: He also made 300 shields of beaten gold, with {{units:about 3 3/4 pounds|three minas}} of gold going into each shield. The king placed them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
en.R: He also made 300 smaller shields of hammered gold. Each one used {{units:about 3 3/4 pounds|three minas}} of gold. The king put them in the great hall called the House of the Forest of Lebanon.

decisions.choice: shields: smaller round shields
decisions.reason: This is the common shield carried on the arm, smaller than the large shield of verse 16.

decisions.choice: three minas: about 150 shekels
decisions.reason: A mina was sixty to a talent, about fifty shekels, so three minas weighed about 3 3/4 pounds. The parallel in 2 Chronicles 9:16 gives "three hundred" of gold for each shield, which may count by a different standard.

decisions.choice: the House of the Forest of Lebanon: Solomon's great hall
decisions.reason: This was the largest of Solomon's palace buildings, named for its rows of cedar pillars from Lebanon (7:2-5). It seems to have served as a hall of state and an armory (Isaiah 22:8).

decisions.choice: He also made (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew continues the list from verse 16 without a verb; Balanced and Readable repeat "made". Readable says "smaller shields" to mark the difference from the large ones.

decisions.choice: the great hall called
decisions.reason: Readable explains that the House of the Forest of Lebanon was a building, not a forest.

source.text: וַיַּ֧עַשׂ הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ כִּסֵּא־שֵׁ֖ן גָּד֑וֹל וַיְצַפֵּ֖הוּ זָהָ֥ב מוּפָֽז׃

records.literal_gloss: And made the king throne of ivory great, and he overlaid it gold refined.

en.L: And the king made a great throne of ivory, and he overlaid it [with] refined gold.
en.B: Then the king made a great ivory throne and overlaid it with the finest gold.
en.R: The king also made a large throne decorated with ivory and covered it with the purest gold.

decisions.choice: a throne of ivory: a throne inlaid with ivory panels
decisions.reason: Ivory was carved into panels and set into wooden furniture; a throne cannot be overlaid with gold if it is solid ivory. "Houses of ivory" were rooms decorated this way (22:39; Amos 3:15).

decisions.choice: refined gold: the finest grade of gold
decisions.reason: The word describes gold of the best quality. It may be linked with "gold of Uphaz" (Jeremiah 10:9); the parallel in 2 Chronicles 9:17 says "pure gold".

decisions.choice: decorated with ivory; covered
decisions.reason: Readable says how the ivory was used and says "covered" for "overlaid".

source.text: שֵׁ֧שׁ מַעֲל֣וֹת לַכִּסֵּ֗ה וְרֹאשׁ־עָגֹ֤ל לַכִּסֵּה֙ מֵאַֽחֲרָ֔יו וְיָדֹ֛ת מִזֶּ֥ה וּמִזֶּ֖ה אֶל־מְק֣וֹם הַשָּׁ֑בֶת וּשְׁנַ֣יִם אֲרָי֔וֹת עֹמְדִ֖ים אֵ֥צֶל הַיָּדֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: Six steps to the throne, and [a] top round to the throne from behind it, and hands from this and from this at [the] place of the sitting, and two lions standing beside the hands.

en.L: Six steps [were] to the throne, and a round top [was] to the throne behind it, and arms [were] on this [side] and on that [side] at the place of the seat, and two lions [were] standing beside the arms.
en.B: The throne had six steps, and the back of the throne had a rounded top. On either side of the seat were armrests, with two lions standing beside the armrests.
en.R: The throne had six steps leading up to it, and its back was rounded at the top. There were armrests on both sides of the seat, and a lion statue stood beside each armrest.

decisions.choice: a round top behind it
alternatives: a calf's head at the back
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word for "round" is very close to the word for "calf". The ancient Greek translation reads "the heads of calves" behind it, a familiar throne design. The Hebrew text reads "round", and it is followed here.

decisions.choice: hands: armrests
decisions.reason: The "hands" of a chair are its arms, the parts on which the sitter's hands rest.

decisions.choice: two lions: a symbol of royal power
decisions.reason: Lions often stood beside royal thrones in the ancient world. In Israel the lion was also the emblem of Judah, Solomon's tribe (Genesis 49:9).

decisions.choice: a lion statue stood beside each armrest
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the lions were carved figures and that there was one at each side.

source.text: וּשְׁנֵ֧ים עָשָׂ֣ר אֲרָיִ֗ים עֹמְדִ֥ים שָׁ֛ם עַל־שֵׁ֥שׁ הַֽמַּעֲל֖וֹת מִזֶּ֣ה וּמִזֶּ֑ה לֹֽא־נַעֲשָׂ֥ה כֵ֖ן לְכָל־מַמְלָכֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And two [and] ten lions standing there on [the] six the steps, from this and from this; not was made thus for any kingdoms.

en.L: And twelve lions [were] standing there on the six steps, on this [side] and on that [side]; nothing like it was made for any kingdom.
en.B: Twelve lions stood there on the six steps, one at each end of each step. Nothing like it had ever been made for any kingdom.
en.R: Twelve lions stood on the six steps, one at each end of every step. No other kingdom had ever had a throne like it.

decisions.choice: twelve lions on the six steps, on this side and on that: a lion at each end of each step
decisions.reason: Six steps with a lion on either side make twelve, besides the two beside the armrests (verse 19).

decisions.choice: nothing like it was made for any kingdom: the throne was without equal
decisions.reason: The phrase claims that no other king had such a throne, part of the chapter's picture of Solomon's surpassing glory (verse 23).

decisions.choice: one at each end of each step
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable spell out the Hebrew "from this and from this", which means on both sides of each step.

source.text: וְ֠כֹל כְּלֵ֞י מַשְׁקֵ֨ה הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה֙ זָהָ֔ב וְכֹ֗ל כְּלֵ֛י בֵּֽית־יַ֥עַר הַלְּבָנ֖וֹן זָהָ֣ב סָג֑וּר אֵ֣ין כֶּ֗סֶף לֹ֥א נֶחְשָׁ֛ב בִּימֵ֥י שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה לִמְאֽוּמָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And all [the] vessels of drinking of the king Solomon [were] gold, and all [the] vessels of [the] house of [the] forest of the Lebanon [were] gold pure; there [was] not silver; not was reckoned in [the] days of Solomon as anything.

en.L: And all the drinking vessels of King Solomon [were] gold, and all the vessels of the house of the forest of Lebanon [were] pure gold; there was no silver; it was not reckoned as anything in the days of Solomon.
en.B: All King Solomon's drinking cups were gold, and all the utensils in the House of the Forest of Lebanon were pure gold. None were silver; in Solomon's days silver was not thought of as anything.
en.R: All of King Solomon's cups were made of gold, and all the dishes in the House of the Forest of Lebanon were pure gold. None of them were silver, because in Solomon's time silver was hardly worth anything.

decisions.choice: pure gold: gold of the best quality
decisions.reason: The word describes gold that has been refined. It is used of the gold in the temple's inner room (6:20-21; 7:49-50).

decisions.choice: silver was not reckoned as anything: there was so much wealth that silver seemed cheap
decisions.reason: This is a deliberate overstatement, like verse 27: silver was so common in Solomon's days that it was not used for the royal tableware.

decisions.choice: because
decisions.reason: Readable joins the two short Hebrew clauses with "because", making explicit why nothing was made of silver.

source.text: כִּי֩ אֳנִ֨י תַרְשִׁ֤ישׁ לַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ בַּיָּ֔ם עִ֖ם אֳנִ֣י חִירָ֑ם אַחַת֩ לְשָׁלֹ֨שׁ שָׁנִ֜ים תָּב֣וֹא׀אֳנִ֣י תַרְשִׁ֗ישׁ נֹֽשְׂאֵת֙ זָהָ֣ב וָכֶ֔סֶף שֶׁנְהַבִּ֥ים וְקֹפִ֖ים וְתֻכִּיִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: For ships of Tarshish [were] to the king at the sea with [the] ships of Hiram; once in three years would come [the] ships of Tarshish carrying gold and silver, ivories, and apes, and peacocks.

en.L: For the king had ships of Tarshish at sea with the ships of Hiram; once in three years the ships of Tarshish would come, carrying gold and silver, ivory, and apes, and peacocks.
en.B: For the king had a fleet of Tarshish ships at sea along with Hiram's fleet. Once every three years the Tarshish ships would come in, bringing gold, silver, ivory, apes and peacocks.
en.R: This was because the king had a fleet of large trading ships at sea along with Hiram's ships. Once every three years they came back loaded with gold, silver, ivory, apes and peacocks.

decisions.choice: ships of Tarshish: large ships built for long voyages
decisions.reason: Tarshish was a far-off port, probably in the far west of the Mediterranean (Jonah 1:3). "Ships of Tarshish" came to mean large seagoing merchant ships of the kind that sailed there, whatever their route: Jehoshaphat built ships of Tarshish to go to Ophir (22:49).

decisions.choice: once in three years: a voyage that took three years to complete
decisions.reason: The ships came back once every three years, which suggests long voyages to distant places.

decisions.choice: ivory, apes, and peacocks: exotic goods whose names are not all certain
decisions.reason: The word for ivory seems to mean "elephant tooth". The word taken as "apes" names some kind of monkey. The last word appears only here and in 2 Chronicles 9:21; it has long been taken as peacocks, but it may name baboons or another kind of monkey.

decisions.choice: This was because; large trading ships
decisions.reason: Readable makes the "for" explicit as the reason for Solomon's wealth in gold, and explains "ships of Tarshish" by the kind of ship they were.

source.text: וַיִּגְדַּל֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה מִכֹּ֖ל מַלְכֵ֣י הָאָ֑רֶץ לְעֹ֖שֶׁר וּלְחָכְמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And became great the king Solomon more than all [the] kings of the earth in wealth and in wisdom.

en.L: And King Solomon became greater than all the kings of the earth in wealth and in wisdom.
en.B: So King Solomon grew greater in riches and in wisdom than all the kings of the earth.
en.R: King Solomon became richer and wiser than any other king on earth.

decisions.choice: wealth and wisdom: what Yahweh promised at Gibeon
decisions.reason: Solomon had asked only for wisdom, and Yahweh promised him riches and honor as well, so that no king would be his equal (3:12-13). This verse records that the promise was kept.

decisions.choice: became greater: Solomon grew to surpass all other kings
decisions.reason: The verb describes Solomon growing great, a process seen through the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: richer and wiser
decisions.reason: Readable turns the two nouns into adjectives, the plainest way to say the same thing.

source.text: וְכָ֨ל־הָאָ֔רֶץ מְבַקְשִׁ֖ים אֶת־פְּנֵ֣י שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה לִשְׁמֹ֨עַ֙ אֶת־חָכְמָת֔וֹ אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֥ן אֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּלִבּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And all the earth [was] seeking [the] face of Solomon to hear his wisdom which put God in his heart.

en.L: And all the earth was seeking the face of Solomon to hear his wisdom, which God had put in his heart.
en.B: The whole earth sought an audience with Solomon, to hear the wisdom God had put in his heart.
en.R: People from all over the world wanted to meet Solomon and hear the wisdom God had given him.

decisions.choice: seeking the face of Solomon: asking to come before him
decisions.reason: To seek a king's face is to seek an audience with him (Proverbs 29:26).

decisions.choice: the wisdom God had put in his heart: wisdom as a gift
decisions.reason: Solomon's wisdom is not his own achievement. God gave it, as he promised (3:12; 5:9). The heart is the seat of understanding.

decisions.choice: The whole earth (Balanced); People from all over the world (Readable)
decisions.reason: "All the earth" means the people of the earth; Readable says so. "Sought an audience" (Balanced) and "wanted to meet" (Readable) explain the idiom of seeking his face.

source.text: וְהֵ֣מָּה מְבִאִ֣ים אִ֣ישׁ מִנְחָת֡וֹ כְּלֵ֣י כֶסֶף֩ וּכְלֵ֨י זָהָ֤ב וּשְׂלָמוֹת֙ וְנֵ֣שֶׁק וּבְשָׂמִ֔ים סוּסִ֖ים וּפְרָדִ֑ים דְּבַר־שָׁנָ֖ה בְּשָׁנָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And they [were] bringing each his gift, articles of silver and articles of gold, and garments, and weaponry, and spices, horses and mules, [the] matter of [a] year in [a] year.

en.L: And they were bringing, each his gift: articles of silver and articles of gold, and garments, and weapons, and spices, horses and mules, a year's portion year by year.
en.B: Each of them brought a gift: articles of silver and gold, robes, weapons and spices, horses and mules, so much every year.
en.R: Year after year, every visitor brought him gifts: things made of silver and gold, clothing, weapons, spices, horses and mules.

decisions.choice: were bringing, year by year: a regular yearly practice
decisions.reason: The verb form describes a continuing custom, and "the matter of a year in a year" means a fixed amount each year. The gifts had the regularity of tribute.

decisions.choice: his gift: an offering to honor the king
decisions.reason: The word is the common word for a gift or offering, used also of tribute paid to a ruler (5:1; Judges 3:15). Visitors seeking Solomon's wisdom came with gifts, as the queen of Sheba did.

decisions.choice: so much every year (Balanced); Year after year (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable express the Hebrew "the matter of a year in a year" in plain English.

source.text: וַיֶּאֱסֹ֣ף שְׁלֹמֹה֮ רֶ֣כֶב וּפָרָשִׁים֒ וַיְהִי־ל֗וֹ אֶ֤לֶף וְאַרְבַּע־מֵאוֹת֙ רֶ֔כֶב וּשְׁנֵים־עָשָׂ֥ר אֶ֖לֶף פָּֽרָשִׁ֑ים וַיַּנְחֵם֙ בְּעָרֵ֣י הָרֶ֔כֶב וְעִם־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And gathered Solomon chariotry and horsemen, and was to him thousand and four hundred chariot[s] and two [and] ten thousand horsemen; and he stationed them in [the] cities of the chariotry and with the king in Jerusalem.

en.L: And Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen; and he had 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horsemen, and he stationed them in the cities of the chariots and with the king in Jerusalem.
en.B: Solomon built up a force of chariots and horsemen. He had 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horsemen, which he stationed in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.
en.R: Solomon built up a large force of chariots and horsemen. He had 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horsemen. He kept some of them in the cities where his chariots were based, and some with him in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: horsemen: the men who rode or drove, or perhaps the horses themselves
decisions.reason: The word usually means horsemen, but it can also mean horses for chariots. The number 12,000 appears again with this word in 5:6, where it stands beside stalls for horses.

decisions.choice: the chariot cities: towns with stables and barracks for the chariot force
decisions.reason: Solomon built store cities and towns for his chariots and horsemen (9:19).

decisions.choice: some ... and some with him
decisions.reason: Readable says that the force was divided between the chariot cities and Jerusalem, and "with him" for "with the king", since the king is Solomon.

source.text: וַיִּתֵּ֨ן הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ אֶת־הַכֶּ֛סֶף בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם כָּאֲבָנִ֑ים וְאֵ֣ת הָאֲרָזִ֗ים נָתַ֛ן כַּשִּׁקְמִ֥ים אֲשֶׁר־בַּשְּׁפֵלָ֖ה לָרֹֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And made the king the silver in Jerusalem like stones, and the cedars he made like the sycamores which [are] in the Shephelah, for abundance.

en.L: And the king made the silver in Jerusalem like stones, and the cedars he made like the sycamores that [are] in the Shephelah, for abundance.
en.B: The king made silver as common in Jerusalem as stones, and he made cedar as plentiful as the sycamore-fig trees of the Shephelah.
en.R: The king made silver as common in Jerusalem as stones. Cedar wood became as plentiful as the fig trees that grow in the western foothills.

decisions.choice: like stones, like the sycamores: a deliberate overstatement
decisions.reason: Stones lay everywhere in the hills of Judah. The verse says, with poetic exaggeration, that silver and costly cedar from Lebanon became as common as the most ordinary things in the land.

decisions.choice: the sycamores in the Shephelah: common fig trees of the low hills
decisions.reason: The sycamore fig is a tree that bears small figs and gives cheap, ordinary timber (Isaiah 9:9; Amos 7:14). The Shephelah is the region of low hills between the coastal plain and the hill country of Judah, where these trees grew in plenty.

decisions.choice: sycamore-fig trees of the Shephelah (Balanced); fig trees that grow in the western foothills (Readable)
decisions.reason: The English "sycamore" names a different tree, so Balanced says "sycamore-fig". Readable explains the Shephelah by where it lies.

source.text: וּמוֹצָ֧א הַסּוּסִ֛ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר לִשְׁלֹמֹ֖ה מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וּמִקְוֵ֕ה סֹחֲרֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ יִקְח֥וּ מִקְוֵ֖ה בִּמְחִֽיר׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] export of the horses which [were] to Solomon [was] from Egypt and from Kue; [the] traders of the king would take [them] from Kue at [a] price.

en.L: And the export of the horses that [were] Solomon's [was] from Egypt and from Kue; the traders of the king would take [them] from Kue at a price.
en.B: Solomon's horses were imported from Egypt and from Kue; the king's traders bought them from Kue at the going price.
en.R: Solomon's horses were brought in from Egypt and from Kue. The king's traders bought them in Kue and paid for them.

decisions.choice: Kue: a land in the south of present-day Turkey
decisions.reason: Kue is known from other ancient records as a land later called Cilicia, famous for its horses. The Hebrew vowels make the name look like a word for "a gathering", and older translations read it as "in droves" or "linen yarn". The place name fits the trade route of verses 28-29.

decisions.choice: Egypt
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says Egypt, which sold chariots (verse 29). Some have suggested that the word here names Musri, a land in Asia Minor near Kue with a similar name, since horses were bred more in the north than in Egypt; but the text as it stands says Egypt, as does Deuteronomy 17:16.

decisions.choice: horses from Egypt: what the law warned a king against
decisions.reason: The law of the king told him not to gather many horses or send the people back to Egypt to get them (Deuteronomy 17:16), nor to gather much silver and gold (17:17). The writer lists Solomon's horses and gold without comment, but the next chapter shows where the king's heart went.

decisions.choice: imported (Balanced); brought in (Readable); bought ... at the going price
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "export" looks at the horses leaving their land; Balanced and Readable look at them arriving in Israel, which is the same trade seen from Solomon's side.

source.text: וַֽ֠תַּעֲלֶה וַתֵּצֵ֨א מֶרְכָּבָ֤ה מִמִּצְרַ֨יִם֙ בְּשֵׁ֣שׁ מֵא֣וֹת כֶּ֔סֶף וְס֖וּס בַּחֲמִשִּׁ֣ים וּמֵאָ֑ה וְ֠כֵן לְכָל־מַלְכֵ֧י הַחִתִּ֛ים וּלְמַלְכֵ֥י אֲרָ֖ם בְּיָדָ֥ם יֹצִֽאוּ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And came up and went out [a] chariot from Egypt for six hundred silver, and [a] horse for fifty and hundred; and thus to all [the] kings of the Hittites and to [the] kings of Aram by their hand they would bring [them] out.

en.L: And a chariot came up and went out from Egypt for 600 [shekels of] silver, and a horse for 150; and so to all the kings of the Hittites and to the kings of Aram, by their hand they would bring [them] out.
en.B: A chariot could be imported from Egypt for {{units:about 15 pounds|600 shekels}} of silver, and a horse for {{units:about 3 3/4 pounds|150 shekels}}. In the same way they exported them, through the king's traders, to all the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Aram.
en.R: A chariot from Egypt cost {{units:about 15 pounds|600 shekels}} of silver, and a horse cost {{units:about 3 3/4 pounds|150 shekels}}. The king's traders also sold horses and chariots to all the kings of the Hittites and of Aram.

decisions.choice: 600 of silver, 150: prices in shekels
decisions.reason: As in verse 16, the Hebrew gives the numbers without the unit; the shekel is understood. A chariot cost four times as much as a horse.

decisions.choice: by their hand they exported: the king's traders sold them on
decisions.reason: "Their hand" refers to the king's traders of verse 28. Solomon's merchants acted as middlemen, buying horses and chariots and selling them to the kingdoms to the north.

decisions.choice: the kings of the Hittites and of Aram: the kingdoms of Syria
decisions.reason: The Hittites here are the small kingdoms of northern Syria that kept the Hittite name after the old Hittite empire fell. Aram is the land of the Arameans, in Syria north and east of Israel.

decisions.choice: 600 [shekels of] silver (Literal); about 15 pounds and about 3 3/4 pounds (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal supplies "shekels" in brackets. Balanced and Readable give the weights in modern measure, with the shekels as the alternative.
